text:
The man prevails. The right-of-way was an easement appurtenant that ended by merger when the woman conveyed the house to him, uniting the dominant and servient estates in one owner, and the later warranty deed of the house alone granted no new easement. No easement by necessity or implication arose: the path was only a more direct route to the highway, and the man never possessed or used the house.
CONFIDENCE: 86
